s: What is hiring external sources for services such as legal, IT and security work earlier done in-house called?
x: Outsourcing means hiring external sources for services previously performed in-house.

s: Contractualisation in public administration is criticised for causing which of the following?
o: Higher job security and stronger unions
Lower job security but stronger unions
Higher job security but weakened unions
Lower job security and weakened unions
x: Contractualisation lowers job security and weakens unions, and may also hurt productivity.

s: What was the main purpose of creating the Civil Services Board in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Regulate online grievance disposal by central ministries
x: The Civil Services Board was created to curb political interference in postings.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about unionisation and contract labour in India?
o: Only about 6.3% of the workforce is unionised
Unionisation in the private sector is about 1.8%
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 requires 10% or 100 workers to form a union
Since 1991, all organised-sector workers have maintained a direct relation with their employer
x: Contractualisation has weakened the direct employer relationship for many organised-sector workers.

s: In which year did the Andhra Pradesh Government set up APCOS, which recruits outsourced staff and pays them directly?
x: APCOS was set up in 2020 to recruit outsourced staff and pay them directly, cutting out contractor middlemen.

s: Contract labour formed about what share of India's manufacturing workforce in 2022-23?
x: Contract labour rose from 20% (1999) to 40.7% (2022-23, ASI) of the manufacturing workforce.

s: To what age has Andhra Pradesh raised the upper age limit for non-uniform direct recruitment, till 30 September 2027?
x: G.O. Ms. No. 187 raised the limit from 42 to 44 years till 30 September 2027.

s: Which recommendation is associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2005–09)?
o: Merger of Group D into Group C
Replacement of pay bands by a pay matrix
Lateral entry at the level of Joint Secretary
x: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry at Joint Secretary level with performance-based appraisal and promotion; the others are Pay Commission features.

s: NITI Aayog's Action Agenda calls for what kind of tenure for lateral entrants?
o: Unstable tenures at the minister's will
x: The Action Agenda supports wider lateral entry at middle and senior levels with longer, stable tenures.

s: Under which scheme are Joint Secretary and Director posts at the Centre ordinarily filled by tenure deputation?
x: These posts are filled through tenure deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme administered by DoPT.

s: In which year did the first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries join at the Union level?
x: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in 2019.

s: In the lateral-entry debate, what is the reservation concern?
o: Reservation is automatically enhanced in every post
Reservation applies only to Director posts
Lateral entrants must be from reserved categories
x: Critics point out that lateral recruitment to single posts carries no reservation, along with conflict of interest and demotivation of career officers.

s: In August 2024, UPSC was told to cancel the lateral-entry advertisement for how many posts?
x: In August 2024, UPSC was told to cancel the lateral-entry advertisement for 45 posts.

s: In a Results Framework Document, what do the targets listed for each ministry serve as?
x: An RFD specifies objectives, success indicators and targets for each ministry; these serve as Key Result Areas.

s: Which body reviews adverse remarks in Annual Confidential Reports?
x: A Referral Board reviews adverse ACR remarks; 360-degree feedback is multi-source appraisal.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: NeSDA – Assessment of digital services for G2C and G2B
Results Framework Document – Uniform assessment framework for States and Union Territories
Good Governance Index – Uniform assessment framework for States and Union Territories
GRAI – Ranking of central ministries on CPGRAMS grievance disposal
x: The Results Framework Document lists ministry objectives, indicators and targets; the uniform framework for States and UTs is the Good Governance Index.

s: In which year was the Results Framework Document introduced?
x: The RFD was introduced in 2009 under the Cabinet Secretariat's PMES.

s: What was India's rank in the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI) 2024?
x: India was ranked 97th in the UN EGDI 2024.

s: How many indicators does GRAI use to rank central ministries on CPGRAMS grievance disposal?
x: GRAI uses 11 indicators grouped into 4 dimensions.

s: In which year was the National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA) first launched?
x: NeSDA, which assesses digital service delivery, was started in 2019.

s: Which of the following is primarily a growth and external-sector measure rather than a measure to reduce the size of the State?
x: Downsizing, disinvestment and privatisation shrink the State's direct role; encouraging FDI is mainly a growth and external-sector measure.

s: What is the sale of part of a PSU's equity to the public called?
x: Disinvestment is selling part of a PSU's equity to the public; it need not transfer ownership or management.

s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed redefining a Government Company so that the State may hold what share of its equity?
x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed a definition under which the State could hold less than 51%, indicating a new paradigm for disinvestment.

s: Which Pay Commission merged Group D into Group C?
x: The Sixth Commission merged Group D into Group C; the Fifth cut staff strength and the Seventh introduced the pay matrix.

s: From which year did the recommendations of the Seventh Pay Commission (Justice A.K. Mathur) become effective?
x: The Seventh Pay Commission reported in 2015, but its recommendations were effective from 2016.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Fifth Pay Commission – S. Ratnavel Pandian
Sixth Pay Commission – S. Ratnavel Pandian
x: The Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Commissions were chaired by Justices S. Ratnavel Pandian, B.N. Srikrishna and A.K. Mathur.

s: Which Pay Commission recommended cutting staff strength by about 30 per cent?
x: The Fifth Pay Commission (1997) recommended a staff cut of about 30 per cent and a freeze on new posts.

s: Which body introduced the pay matrix in place of pay bands?
x: The Seventh Pay Commission replaced the Sixth Commission's running pay bands with a pay matrix.

s: Who chaired the Sixth Central Pay Commission?
x: The Sixth Pay Commission (2008) was chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna; it merged Group D into Group C.

s:
Which of the following are features of New Public Management?
1. Performance auditing
2. Contracting out non-core services
3. Rejection of all performance measures
x: NPM promotes performance auditing, contracting out and a customer view of citizens; it does not reject performance measurement.

s:
Which of the following were pioneering countries of New Public Management?
1. United Kingdom
2. New Zealand
3. Australia
x: The UK under Thatcher, New Zealand, Australia and the USA are identified as NPM pioneers.

s: Which of the following is a doctrine of Christopher Hood's New Public Management?
o: Complete elimination of competition in the public sector
Emphasis on process and input controls
x: Hood's NPM doctrines include hands-on professional management, explicit performance standards, output controls and competition in the public sector.

s: Who popularised the term 'New Public Management' in 1991?
x: Christopher Hood popularised NPM in 1991; Osborne and Gaebler wrote Reinventing Government (1992).

s: In Reinventing Government, the principle 'steer rather than row' describes which kind of government?
x: Catalytic government steers rather than rows; community-owned government empowers, competitive injects competition, mission-driven moves from rules to mission.

s: In the Reinventing Government framework, moving from hierarchy to participation and teamwork is the meaning of which principle?
x: The decentralised principle seeks to move from hierarchy to participation and teamwork.

s: 'Prevent rather than cure' describes which principle of Reinventing Government?
x: Anticipatory government means prevent rather than cure; enterprising means earn rather than spend.

s: Who are the authors of 'Reinventing Government' (1992)?
x: David Osborne and Ted Gaebler wrote Reinventing Government (1992), with the idea 'steering, not rowing'.

s: Which principle of Reinventing Government means 'earn rather than spend'?
x: Enterprising government earns rather than spends; catalytic government steers rather than rows.

s: How is the New Public Service response to treating the citizen merely as a customer expressed?
x: New Public Service answers the citizen-as-customer view with 'serve, not steer', stressing citizenship rights, equity and accountability.

s: 'Serve, not steer' is the central prescription of which approach?
x: New Public Service emphasises democratic citizenship and public interest, and holds that administrators should serve, not steer.

s: What is the core claim of Public Value theory?
o: Public managers should pursue efficiency alone
Citizens should be treated only as customers
Public managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust
x: Public Value theory holds that managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust, not merely efficiency.

s: Who is the author of 'Creating Public Value' (1995)?
x: Mark Moore wrote Creating Public Value (1995), holding that value includes legitimacy and trust.

s: Citizens' Charters, service standards and grievance redressal are instruments of which idea?
x: Treating the citizen as a customer uses Citizens' Charters, service standards and grievance redressal.

s: The main criticism of treating the citizen merely as a customer is that the citizen:
o: Has rights, not just purchasing power
Should be served only by contractors
Has purchasing power but no rights
x: Critics say the citizen has rights, not just purchasing power, and that equity and accountability suffer.

s: Who propounded the 'New Public Service' approach?
x: New Public Service, with the slogan 'serve, not steer', is by Denhardt and Denhardt; Mark Moore wrote Creating Public Value.

s: Which of the following is included in the ‘core of the core’ category of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
x: MGNREGA is included in the core-of-the-core category, along with NSAP and umbrella schemes for vulnerable groups.

s: PMMVY and ICDS follow which Centre-State sharing ratio?
x: PMMVY and ICDS follow a 60:40 Centre-State sharing pattern.

s: After the 2015 rationalisation, core Centrally Sponsored Schemes are mostly funded in which Centre:State ratio?
x: Core schemes are mostly funded 60:40; the 90:10 ratio applies only to North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

s: At about what annual rate have Centrally Sponsored Schemes grown since 2016-17?
x: CSS grew about 26.5% a year since 2016-17, while State plan allocations fell by nearly 30%.

s: For which States are core Centrally Sponsored Schemes funded in the Centre:State ratio of 90:10?
o: States with a fiscal deficit above 3% of GSDP
x: Core CSS are mostly 60:40, but 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

s: Which body recommended the rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes into core of the core, core and optional schemes in 2015?
o: Sub-Group of Chief Ministers of NITI Aayog
x: In 2015 a NITI Aayog Sub-Group of Chief Ministers rationalised CSS into core of the core, core and optional groups.

s: Which of the following is generally regarded as a symbol of cooperative federalism?
x: The GST Council, where the Centre and States decide jointly, is generally regarded as a symbol of cooperative federalism.

s: The 16th Finance Commission’s introduction of a GDP-contribution criterion is intended to promote which form of federalism?
x: The GDP-contribution criterion rewards efficiency and has been described as part of a framework for competitive and accountable federalism.

s: Which body prepares the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) ranking of States?
x: BRAP state rankings are prepared by DPIIT, first in 2015.

s: Which State ranked first in BRAP 2019, released in September 2020?
x: Andhra Pradesh was first in BRAP 2019, with Uttar Pradesh second and Telangana third.

s: Which of the following mainly made States compete for private and foreign investment after 1991?
x: Post-1991 delicensing made States compete for private and foreign investment.

s: Which body is regarded as a symbol of competitive federalism, having replaced the Planning Commission's allocation role?
x: NITI Aayog symbolises competitive federalism; the GST Council symbolises cooperative federalism.

s: In which year did DPIIT first release the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) ranking of States?
x: DPIIT's BRAP ranking of States was first released in 2015.

s: Which of the following represents the divergence view of regional disparities after the 1991 reforms?
o: Richer and industrialised States attracted most post-1991 private investment, widening regional gaps.
Transfers completely eliminated differences between States.
Poorer States automatically caught up because private investment was evenly distributed.
Infrastructure investment was concentrated only in poorer States.
x: The divergence view holds that richer, industrialised States attracted a larger share of post-1991 private investment, causing regional gaps to widen.

s: Fiscal transfers try to correct regional imbalances, but over which of the following do disputes mainly arise?
x: Transfers aim to correct imbalances, but the horizontal criteria for sharing among States spark disputes.

s: Which of the following pairs (Finance Commission – fact) is correctly matched?
x: The 15th FC under N.K. Singh recommended 41%, one point below the 14th FC's 42%.

s: The 15th Finance Commission covered which period?
x: The 15th FC covered 2020–26 in two reports; 2015–20 was the 14th FC's period.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent figures on cesses and tax devolution?
o: Actual devolution in 2025-26 was close to the full 41% share
About 18% of gross tax revenue was in cesses in 2025-26
These cesses are not shareable with the States
The 16th Finance Commission kept the devolution share at 41% for 2026-31
x: Because about 18% of gross tax revenue was in non-shareable cesses, actual devolution was nearer 31-32%, not 41%.

s: Southern States protested in 2024 that population weights in devolution:
o: Rewarded States with better performance disproportionately
x: Southern States argued that population weights punish good performance in the devolution formula.

s: Who chairs the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31)?
x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th.

s: What change did the 14th Finance Commission make to the States' share of net divisible taxes?
x: The 14th FC raised the States' share from 32% to 42%, a 10-point rise.

s: What vertical share did the 16th Finance Commission recommend for the States, as accepted in Budget 2026-27?
x: The 16th FC retained the 41% share, accepted in Budget 2026-27; 42% was the 14th FC's share.

s: Who chaired the 14th Finance Commission?
x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC (2015-20), which raised the States' share from 32% to 42%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the FRBM Act targets (as amended in 2018)?
o: Central government debt of not more than 60% of GDP by 31 March 2025
Fiscal deficit of not more than 3% of GDP by 31 March 2021
The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003
General government debt of not more than 60% of GDP by 31 March 2025
x: The Central government debt target is 40% of GDP; 60% is the target for general government debt.

s: Under Article 293(3) of the Constitution, a State indebted to the Centre requires whose consent to borrow further?
o: Consent of the President acting alone
x: A State that is indebted to the Centre requires the consent of the Union Government to borrow under Article 293(3).

s: The Centre steers State capital expenditure through which mechanism mentioned in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
x: The Centre steers State capital expenditure through SASCI.

s: In State of Kerala v. Union of India (2024), Kerala filed a suit under which Article to challenge the Centre's Net Borrowing Ceiling?
x: Kerala used the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction in Centre-State disputes under Article 131 to challenge the Net Borrowing Ceiling, which counts off-budget borrowings against the State's cap. Article 32 is for enforcing Fundamental Rights; Article 226 is High Court writ jurisdiction; Article 293 is the borrowing provision itself (293(3) needs Central consent), not the route to sue.

s: What did the 16th Finance Commission recommend on State fiscal deficits?
x: The 16th FC capped State deficits at 3% of GSDP, ended off-budget borrowing and asked for subsidy rationalisation.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the four statements laid in Parliament under the FRBM Act?
x: The four FRBM statements are Medium-term Fiscal Policy, Fiscal Policy Strategy, Macro-economic Framework and Medium-term Expenditure Framework.

s: Under the FRBM Act (amended 2018), Central government debt was to be brought down to what share of GDP by 2025?
x: The target was 40% of GDP for Central debt and 60% for general government debt.

s: In the GST Council, what share of the votes does the Centre hold?
x: The Centre holds one-third of the votes and all States together two-thirds.

s: What majority do decisions of the GST Council need?
x: GST Council decisions need a three-fourths weighted majority, so the Centre alone cannot pass one.

s:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. It is provided for under Article 279A.
2. It was inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
3. The Centre alone can pass a decision of the Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Council rests on Article 279A (101st CAA, 2016); with only one-third of the votes the Centre cannot pass a decision alone.

s: From which date was the GST compensation cess discontinued for most goods?
x: The 5-year compensation ended in June 2022, the cess was extended to repay COVID-era loans, and it was discontinued for most goods from 22 September 2025.

s: What education spending target did NEP 2020 set?
x: NEP 2020 set an education target of 6% of GDP; 2.5% was the NHP 2017 public health target.

s: Excessive expenditure on unconditional cash schemes by some states is criticised primarily because it may crowd out spending on which sectors?
o: Defence, foreign affairs and space research
x: Some states reportedly spend over 200% of their health budget on cash schemes, raising concern that health, education and nutrition spending may be crowded out.

s:
Consider the following statements about social sector spending in India:
1. Social protection spending is only about 4.0% of GDP.
2. States bear 75.2% of school education spending.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Social protection is just 4.0% of GDP, and States bear 75.2% of school education spending.

s: What public health spending target did the National Health Policy 2017 set?
x: NHP 2017 targeted public health spending of 2.5% of GDP; 6% is the NEP 2020 education target.

s: What is PAHAL?
o: Direct transfer of fertiliser subsidy to farmers
Direct transfer of LPG subsidy through Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts
Guaranteed wage employment in rural areas
x: PAHAL is a DBT mechanism for LPG subsidy using Aadhaar-seeded accounts.

s: JAM-based welfare delivery is criticised because it may:
o: Exclude persons lacking digital access or required documents
Raise the States' share of MGNREGA funding
x: JAM streamlines delivery but can exclude those without digital access or documents; it does not eliminate exclusion.

s: On which date did Direct Benefit Transfer begin in India?
x: DBT began on 1 January 2013.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MGNREGA?
o: It provides 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household
Its funding is roughly 90:10 between the Centre and the States
It is confined to urban households
x: MGNREGA concerns rural households, so the last statement is false; the 100 days and the 90:10 funding are correct.

s: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what share of the rural population?
x: NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population, with 5 kg of grain per person per month.

s: The shift from enforceable welfare rights to discretionary transfers is criticised on the ground that it:
o: transfers all welfare functions to local governments
makes all welfare benefits universal and automatic
x: The criticism is that discretionary transfers can transform citizens who hold enforceable rights into passive beneficiaries.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Food Security Act, 2013?
o: It covers up to 75% of the rural population
It covers up to 50% of the urban population
It gives 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month
It gives 10 kg of grain per household per month
x: NFSA gives 5 kg per person per month, not 10 kg per household.

s: The VB-G RAM G Act replaced which welfare law?
x: The VB-G RAM G Act replaced MGNREGA and raises the States' contribution.

s: In which year did disinvestment revenue rise, when it fell in every other year?
x: Apart from a surge in 2022-23, disinvestment revenue has fallen, while dividends have grown every year.

s: What is a disinvestment transaction in which both a stake and management control are transferred called?
x: A strategic sale involves the transfer of a stake together with management control. The other methods do not necessarily transfer control.

s: In disinvestment, with whom does an Institutional Placement Programme (IPP) place shares?
x: IPP refers to placement only with Qualified Institutional Buyers.

s: What does the government do in minority disinvestment?
o: Transfers management control to a partner
x: Minority disinvestment leaves the government above 51% with control; majority disinvestment and strategic sale transfer control.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy, 2021?
o: Maintaining a bare-minimum presence in strategic sectors
Retaining a Government enterprise in every non-strategic sector
x: The policy envisages exit from non-strategic sectors, not retention of a Government enterprise in every such sector. It retains only a bare-minimum presence in strategic sectors.

s: Which of the following is one of the four strategic sector groups under the New PSE Policy, 2021?
x: The four groups are atomic energy, space and defence; transport and telecom; power, petroleum, coal and minerals; and banking, insurance and financial services.

s: What was significant about the LIC Initial Public Offer of 17 May 2022?
o: the first complete privatisation of a CPSE
India's biggest issue at that time
the first OFS conducted by DIPAM
x: The LIC IPO on 17 May 2022 was India's biggest issue at that time.

s: Which department manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs and conducts disinvestment?
o: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
x: DIPAM, under the Ministry of Finance, manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs and conducts disinvestment.

s: When was the Department of Disinvestment, later renamed DIPAM, set up?
x: The Department of Disinvestment was set up on 10 December 1999 and renamed DIPAM on 14 April 2016.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about DIPAM?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Finance
It manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs
It got its present name on 14 April 2016
It functions under the Ministry of Commerce
x: DIPAM is under the Ministry of Finance, not the Ministry of Commerce.

s: Who makes a Follow-on Public Offer (FPO) in disinvestment?
o: A PSE issuing shares for the first time
x: An IPO is a PSE's first issue; an FPO is made by an already listed PSE.

s: Since which year has the Offer for Sale (OFS) route been used for disinvestment?
x: The OFS method of selling shares of listed PSEs has been used since 2012.

s: How does BOT (Annuity) differ from BOT (Toll)?
o: The government pays a fixed annuity and bears the revenue risk
The private player bears the revenue risk
The private player owns the asset permanently
Toll rights on an already-built highway are transferred
x: In BOT (Annuity) the government pays a fixed annuity and bears revenue risk; in BOT (Toll) the private player bears it.

s: In which PPP model does the private player own the asset during the concession period and subsequently transfer it to the government?
x: BOOT stands for Build-Own-Operate-Transfer; the private player owns the asset during the concession and transfers it thereafter.

s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model, the government pays what share of the project cost during construction?
x: Under HAM the government pays 40% during construction; the developer's 60% is repaid through annuities over about 15 years.

s: Under the EPC model, who funds the project?
x: Under EPC the government provides all funding and the private player only constructs.

s: Under which PPP model are toll rights on already-built highways transferred to private players?
x: TOT means Toll-Operate-Transfer and involves transferring toll rights on already-built highways to private players.

s: In which of the following was the Hybrid Annuity Model first used outside the roads sector?
x: Namami Gange STPs pioneered HAM outside roads, with performance-linked payments under the One City One Operator model.

s: What is the full form of BOLT?
x: BOLT is Build-Own-Lease-Transfer: the asset is leased to the government and then transferred.

s: In which PPP model does the private partner design, build, finance and operate the project?
x: DBFO(T) is Design-Build-Finance-Operate-(Transfer); EPC is government-funded construction only.

s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model, over about how many years is the developer's 60% share repaid through semi-annual annuities?
x: In HAM the government pays 40% during construction and repays the developer's 60% through annuities over about 15 years.

s: In 2026, to what level did MoRTH raise the net-worth requirement for bidders in Hybrid Annuity Model projects?
x: MoRTH (2026) raised the HAM net-worth requirement from 15% to 20%.

s: What does the AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001 primarily provide?
o: The constitutional basis for privatisation of all State enterprises
The statutory framework for Union disinvestment of CPSEs
The legal framework exclusively for municipal bonds
The legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh, including Swiss-challenge proposals
x: The AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001 provides the legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh and includes Swiss-challenge proposals.

s: The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks how much for Viability Gap Funding?
x: The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks ₹1,500 crore for VGF and proposes a bridge fund.

s:
Consider the following about PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Gangavaram is an airport developed by GMR.
2. Krishnapatnam Port was acquired by Adani Ports in 2020.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Krishnapatnam Port, built under PPP, was acquired by Adani Ports in 2020; Gangavaram is not a GMR airport.

s: Who is developing Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Bhogapuram airport is a GMR project on DBFOT with a 40-year concession.

s: In which year did Adani Ports acquire Gangavaram Port?
x: Adani Ports acquired Gangavaram Port in 2021 and Krishnapatnam Port in 2020.

s: Under which PPP model is Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh being developed by GMR?
x: Bhogapuram airport is a DBFOT project with GMR on a 40-year concession.

s: For how many years is the concession for Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh?
x: GMR is developing Bhogapuram airport on DBFOT basis under a 40-year concession.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is Krishnapatnam Port located?
x: Krishnapatnam Port is in Nellore district; it was acquired by Adani Ports in 2020.

s: Which transactions represented the shift towards strategic sales during 1999–2004?
o: Air India and Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd
x: The policy moved towards strategic sales during 1999–2004, with VSNL and BALCO cited as examples. Until 1999–2000, only minority stakes had been sold.

s: Which of the following pairs (enterprise – buyer) is correctly matched?
x: VSNL went to the Tata group; Modern Foods to Hindustan Lever, BALCO to Sterlite and Air India to Talace (Tata Sons).

s:
Consider the following about Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd:
1. Its sale generated proceeds for the exchequer.
2. It was acquired by a Tata group steel entity.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: NINL was acquired by a Tata group steel entity; the Centre got no proceeds because it held no equity.

s: To whom was Modern Foods sold in 2000, India's first strategic sale?
x: Modern Foods was sold to Hindustan Lever (74%) in 2000, the first strategic sale.

s: To whom was Air India sold in January 2022?
x: Air India went to Talace, a Tata Sons company, in January 2022.

s: To whom was BALCO strategically sold in 2001?
x: BALCO went to Sterlite (Vedanta) with 51% in 2001.

s: The Kelkar Committee on PPP recommended discouraging whom from bidding for toll PPPs?
x: The report proposed discouraging PSUs from bidding for toll PPPs, not barring private participation.

s: Which pair of institutions was proposed to expedite dispute resolution and project review in PPPs?
x: The Kelkar Committee (2015) proposed IPAT, the Infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal headed by a former SC/HC judge, and IPRC, the Infrastructure PPP Project Review Committee, to speed up dispute resolution and project review. The ETFs are disinvestment instruments, DIPAM/DPE are departments, and NMP/VGF are monetisation and funding schemes.

s: With which recommendations was the Vijay Kelkar Committee (2012) associated?
o: exclusion of CPSE subsidiaries from performance agreements
replacement of the MoU system by annual budgeting
x: The Vijay Kelkar Committee recommended faster disinvestment and governance reforms.

s: What did the Kelkar Committee recommend that PPP contracts should have?
o: A mandatory Swiss challenge in every project
A complete prohibition on any contractual modification
x: Because unforeseen financial and implementation problems can arise, the Kelkar Committee wanted a built-in mechanism for renegotiation of PPP contracts.

s: In which year was the Disinvestment Commission headed by G.V. Ramakrishna established?
x: The Disinvestment Commission, headed by G.V. Ramakrishna, was established in 1996.

s: Which committee recommended that disinvestment in PSUs reserved for the public sector could extend up to 49%?
x: The C. Rangarajan Committee in 1993 recommended disinvestment up to 49% in PSUs reserved for the public sector, along with wider ownership and listing.

s:
Consider the following about asset monetisation:
1. It involves the permanent sale of those assets.
2. It earns revenue from under-utilised public assets through private participation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Asset monetisation generates revenue from under-utilised public assets through private participation without permanently selling them.

s: Through which of the following does asset monetisation transfer rights for a limited period?
x: Asset monetisation transfers rights for a limited period by lease or licence, and the assets ordinarily return to the government.

s: When did NITI Aayog launch the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) 1.0?
x: NITI Aayog launched NMP 1.0 in August 2021 with a size of about ₹6 lakh crore.

s: Which of the following represents a criticism of asset monetisation and disinvestment?
o: Assets may be undervalued, and monetisation may be viewed as a sale by another name.
Strategic sales always increase Government ownership and control.
Dividends have disappeared completely from public enterprises.
Asset monetisation eliminates all concerns about valuation.
x: Criticisms include possible undervaluation of assets and the perception that monetisation is a sale by another name. The shift from disinvestment towards dividends is also debated.

s: Asset monetisation lets public asset owners use which financial structures?
x: Asset monetisation enables use of Infrastructure Investment Trusts and Real Estate Investment Trusts; the others are disinvestment methods.

s: What is the size of the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (FY26-FY30)?
x: NMP 2.0 is ₹16.72 lakh crore, of which ₹5.8 lakh crore is private; NMP 1.0 was about ₹6 lakh crore.

s: Which sector has the largest share in NMP 2.0?
x: Highways lead NMP 2.0 with 26%, followed by power 17%, railways and ports 16% each, and coal 13%.

s: Which assets does the National Monetisation Pipeline cover?
x: NMP covers brownfield public assets only, with rights given for a limited period; it is not a sale.

s: How many sectors are covered under the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0?
x: NMP 2.0 (FY26-FY30) covers 12 sectors, led by highways at 26%.

s: What was the size of the National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0 (FY22-FY25)?
x: NMP 1.0, launched by NITI Aayog in August 2021, was about Rs 6 lakh crore; Rs 16.72 lakh crore is NMP 2.0.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme?
o: It provides a capital grant for commercially viable PPP projects
The sponsoring authority may add up to a further 20%
The Centre may provide up to 20% of the project cost
For social-sector projects, the limits may rise to 30% each
x: VGF is a capital grant for PPP projects that are economically justified but commercially unviable.

s: Which institution appraises central-sector public-private partnership projects and is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs?
x: The PPP Appraisal Committee appraises central-sector PPP projects and is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs.

s: What share does the Centre hold in the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF)?
x: NIIF (2015) is a quasi-sovereign fund in which the Centre holds 49%.

s: What does IIFCL (2006) mainly provide?
x: IIFCL provides long-term infrastructure debt; VGF gives grants and PPPAC appraises central PPPs.

s: Under the VGF scheme, what share of project cost does the Centre normally give as grant for a PPP outside the social sector?
x: VGF gives 20% from the Centre plus 20% from the sponsor; 30% + 30% in the social sector.

s: Which of the following is a major cause of stalled PPP projects?
o: Aggressive bidding, revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays
Automatic transfer of all risks to the Government
Guaranteed traffic growth and absence of land issues
Exclusive reliance on dividend income from CPSEs
x: Aggressive bidding, often producing the winner's curse, traffic and revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays can leave PPP projects stalled.

s: Under the Swiss-challenge method, what does the Government do after receiving an unsolicited proposal?
o: Refers it to the Finance Commission
Converts it into an EPC contract
x: The Swiss-challenge method invites counter-bids after an unsolicited proposal; the Kelkar Committee (2015) discouraged it.

s: Under the Swiss-challenge method, which of the following is true of the original proponent after counter-bids are received?
x: The Swiss challenge lets the original proponent match the best counter-bid; it is criticised for information asymmetry.

s: What is aggressive bidding that leads to stalled PPP projects often called?
x: Aggressive bidding (the winner's curse) and traffic shortfalls stall projects and lead to renegotiation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
x: Zonal Councils are statutory; the FC, ECI and Inter-State Council rest on Articles of the Constitution.

s: Under which Article does the President set up the Inter-State Council?
x: Article 263 empowers the President to set up the Inter-State Council, first set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.

s: Which of the following is a statutory body, not a constitutional one?
x: The CIC is statutory, under the RTI Act, 2005; the ECI (Art. 324) and the Finance Commission (Art. 280) are constitutional.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Election Commission of India?
x: Article 324 provides for the Election Commission; 315 is for PSCs and 280 for the Finance Commission.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
x: Article 148 provides for the CAG, who holds office for 6 years or up to 65 years of age.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions?
x: Article 315 provides for the UPSC and SPSCs; Article 317 deals with removal of their members.

s: From which Act do the Water Disputes Tribunals derive their statutory basis?
x: Water Disputes Tribunals are statutory bodies established under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, in the context of Article 262.

s: Under which Act was the North Eastern Council established as a statutory body?
x: The North Eastern Council was established as a statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971.

s: What is the status of the National Security Council of India?
o: A statutory body set up under an Act of Parliament in 1998
An extra-constitutional body set up by an executive order in 1998
A statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971
x: The National Security Council is an extra-constitutional body created by an executive order in 1998; it has neither constitutional nor statutory basis.

s: Under which of the following were Zonal Councils set up?
x: Zonal Councils derive from the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, whereas the NDC and Planning Commission came from executive resolutions.

s: Zonal Councils were created under which Section of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under Section 15 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956; the Inter-State Council rests on Article 263.

s: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is under Article 350B; NITI Aayog is executive and the NCM and NHRC are statutory.

s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of constitutional status?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
x: The NCBC, CAG and Finance Commission are constitutional bodies. NITI Aayog is an executive, non-statutory body created by Cabinet resolution.

s: On whose recommendation was the Inter-State Council set up in 1990?
x: The President set up the Inter-State Council under Article 263 in 1990 on the advice of the Sarkaria Commission.

s: By which of the following can a statutory body be altered?
x: A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament and can be altered by amending that Act.

s: Which of the following is an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body?
x: The Law Commission is set up from time to time by executive order, so it is extra-constitutional. The SC Commission, Finance Commission and State Election Commission are constitutional.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Planning Commission?
o: It was created by a Government resolution
It was chaired by the Prime Minister
The States were not represented in it
It was a constitutional body under Article 263
x: The Planning Commission was an advisory body set up by Government resolution, not a constitutional body.

s: In which year was the Planning Commission set up by a Government resolution?
x: The Planning Commission was set up by a resolution of 15 March 1950; the NDC followed in 1952.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State-level bodies?
o: State Finance Commissions are provided for under Articles 243I and 243Y
A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by Parliament at the request of two or more States
A Joint State Public Service Commission is a statutory body
State Information Commissions are constitutional bodies under Article 315
x: State Information Commissions are statutory bodies under the RTI Act, 2005, not constitutional bodies.

s: By which of the following is a Joint State Public Service Commission created?
x: Article 315 enables a JSPSC, but the body itself is statutory, created by Parliament.

s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up?
x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990; the ECI dates from 1950, the First Finance Commission 1951 and the NDC 1952.

s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the establishment years of the Inter-State Council, NCM and NHRC?
x: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990, the NCM in 1992 and the NHRC in 1993.

s: What is a body created by a resolution or executive order called?
x: Executive bodies rest on a resolution or executive order; constitutional bodies on an Article, statutory ones on an Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT a statutory body?
x: The CBI is non-statutory; it draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946. CVC, NCW and NGT have their own Acts.

s: The Law Commission of India reports to which ministry?
x: The Law Commission is an advisory research body that recommends to the Government and reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice.

s: What is the term of the 23rd Law Commission of India?
x: The 23rd Law Commission runs from 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2027; each Law Commission has a 3-year term.

s: Justice A.R. Lakshmanan was the Chairman of which Law Commission of India?
x: Justice A.R. Lakshmanan, a retired Supreme Court judge, chaired the 18th Law Commission (till 2009).

s: Who was the Chairman of the Law Commission that issued a questionnaire on the Uniform Civil Code in October 2016?
x: The 21st Law Commission, chaired by Justice B.S. Chauhan, released the UCC questionnaire on 7 October 2016.

s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission of India in April 2025?
x: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Dinesh Maheshwari became Chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission from April 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Law Commission of India:
1. It can take up research on a subject suo motu.
2. It can take up subjects referred to it by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Law Commission works on references from the Central Government and can also take up studies suo motu.

s: Which of the following is a statutory body?
x: The NHRC rests on an Act of Parliament; the CAG and FC are constitutional and NITI Aayog is executive.

s:
Assertion (A): The Attorney General of India holds office during the pleasure of the President.
Reason (R): The Attorney General is qualified to be a Judge of the Supreme Court.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: the Attorney General serves at the President's pleasure and must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge. The qualification does not explain the tenure, so R does not explain A.

s: Which of the following bodies has civil court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records?
x: The NCBC has powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses and requisitioning records, particularly after it received constitutional status in 2018.

s: Besides a chairperson and a vice-chairperson, the National Commission for Minorities has how many members?
x: The NCM has a chairperson, a vice-chairperson and five members; five of the seven must be from notified minorities.

s: The National Commission for Minorities functions under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The NCM is a statutory body that functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.

s: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission set up on 12 October under the Protection of Human Rights Act?
x: The NHRC was set up on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; it is a statutory body.

s: From which of the following does the CBI derive its powers?
x: The CBI is non-statutory in itself; it draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946 and is associated with the DoPT.

s: Under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, the CBI generally requires which of the following to act in a State?
o: Sanction of the Governor of the State
Prior consent of the concerned State Government
Approval of the concerned High Court
Consent of the Supreme Court in every case
x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires the consent of the concerned State Government; several States have withdrawn general consent.

s: The origin of the Central Bureau of Investigation is associated with which committee and period?
x: The origin of the CBI is associated with the Santhanam Committee of 1962–63.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: National Commission for Minorities — Ministry of Minority Affairs
National Human Rights Commission — Ministry of Home Affairs
National Commission for Women — Ministry of Women and Child Development
National Green Tribunal — Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
x: The National Green Tribunal is associated with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

s: The National Green Tribunal comes under which ministry?
x: The NGT (NGT Act, 2010) is under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not MeitY.

s: In which year was the Central Vigilance Commission first set up by a resolution?
x: The CVC was first set up by a 1964 resolution and became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003.

s: After 2019, what is the term of the NHRC Chairperson and members?
x: Since 2019 the NHRC term is 3 years or 70 years of age; earlier it was 5 years.

s: Which of the following pairs (body – parent Act) is correctly matched?
x: The Press Council Act is of 1978; Lokpal is under the 2013 Act, UIDAI the 2016 Aadhaar Act and the NGT the 2010 Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Commission for Minorities?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs
It was set up under the NCM Act, 1992
It is a constitutional body under Article 350-B
x: The NCM is statutory (1992 Act); Article 350-B is the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

s: Who among the following select the Director of the CBI?
o: President, Prime Minister and Home Minister
Prime Minister, Home Minister and Central Vigilance Commissioner
Chief Justice of India, Speaker and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India (or nominee) and Leader of the Opposition
x: A committee of the PM, the CJI or a nominated judge, and the Leader of the Opposition selects the CBI Director.

s: Under which Act was the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) constituted?
x: The CBDT is a statutory body under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963, in the Ministry of Finance.

s: Who was the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026?
x: Harjit Singh Grewal was the NCM chairperson as of July 2026.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a quasi-judicial body?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
x: NITI Aayog is an advisory body and is not quasi-judicial. NHRC, SEBI and CIC are examples of bodies having quasi-judicial features.

s: Which of the following can a quasi-judicial body do?
o: Exercise the complete jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
Interpret and apply law under statutory authority
x: A quasi-judicial body is not a court, but it can interpret and apply law, summon persons and impose sanctions under statutory authority.

s: Which of the following is an example of a quasi-judicial body?
x: The Mental Health Review Commission, like the NHRC, SEBI and CIC, is quasi-judicial; the others are advisory.

s: Which of the following has civil court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records?
x: The NCST, NCSC, NCBC and CIC have civil court powers; NITI Aayog and the Law Commission are advisory.

s: In which year was the Act governing the National Commission for Women passed?
x: The NCW Act is of 1990; 1992 is the NCM Act and 1993 the Protection of Human Rights Act.

s: The National Commission for Backward Classes (Article 338B) got constitutional status through which Amendment?
x: NCBC came from the 102nd Amendment, 2018; the 89th created NCST and the 101st the GST Council.

s: In the order of precedence, which of the following groups is placed at rank 9A?
o: Chairperson of UPSC, Chief Election Commissioner and Comptroller and Auditor General
Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST
Chairperson of the Finance Commission, Attorney General and Cabinet Secretary
Chairpersons of the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission
x: The Chairperson of the UPSC, the Chief Election Commissioner and the CAG are placed at rank 9A in the order of precedence. The Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST are placed at rank 17.

s: The CAG holds office for six years or up to what age, whichever is earlier?
x: The CAG (Article 148) serves six years or until age 65, and is removed like a Supreme Court judge.

s: Under Article 317, who alone can remove the members of the UPSC and SPSC?
x: Under Article 317, members of both the UPSC and State PSCs can be removed only by the President, after a Supreme Court inquiry. The Governor appoints State PSC members but cannot remove them.

s: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The 7th Amendment (1956) inserted the linguistic minorities officer; the 65th set up the joint SC/ST Commission and the 89th split off the NCST.

s: Who determines the qualifications of members of the Finance Commission?
x: The President appoints the members, but Parliament determines their qualifications by law.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
x: The NCST is under Article 338-A; the NCSC is under 338, the NCBC under 338-B and the linguistic minorities officer under 350-B.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Chief Election Commissioner – Removed in the same manner as a High Court Judge
State Finance Commission – Constituted every five years
State Election Commissioner – Removed in the same manner as a High Court Judge
CAG – Six years or 65 years, whichever is earlier
x: The CEC is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court Judge.

s: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The President appoints the Election Commissioners
The President appoints the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Members of the National Commission for Backward Classes are appointed by the Prime Minister
The President appoints the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
x: The NCBC, like the ECI, NCSC, NCST and the linguistic minorities officer, is appointed by the President.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Finance Commission submits its report to the President.
The report is laid along with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.
The Finance Minister lays the Finance Commission report before Parliament.
The President causes the report to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
x: Under Article 281 the President, not the Finance Minister, causes the Finance Commission report to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, with an explanatory memorandum on action taken. The other statements are correct.

s: The Chief Election Commissioner is removed in the same manner as which of the following?
x: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge, not a High Court judge.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment provided for the GST Council?
x: The GST Council (Art. 279A) came with the 101st CAA, 2016.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Attorney General of India?
x: The AG is under Article 76; Article 165 is the Advocate General, 148 the CAG and 280 the Finance Commission.

s: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner and the Advocate General; the President appoints the Attorney General and the Finance Commission.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Advocate General of a State?
x: Article 165 covers the Advocate General; 76 is the Attorney General, 148 the CAG and 280 the Finance Commission.

s: Whose finances does the State Finance Commission review?
x: The State Finance Commission reviews the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities; it is constituted by the Governor.

s: What does the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 recommend?
o: Allocation of Plan funds to Union Ministries
Rates of GST on goods and services
Distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States
Borrowing limits of the States under Article 293
x: The Finance Commission recommends how the net proceeds of taxes are shared between the Union and the States.

s: Under which of the following are State Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes established?
x: State SC and ST Commissions are set up under State laws; they are not directly created by Articles 338 and 338A.

s: State Election Commissions are provided for under which Articles?
x: State Election Commissions fall under Articles 243-K and 243-ZA; 243-I and 243-Y cover State Finance Commissions.

s: Under which of the following are State Information Commissions set up?
x: State Information Commissions are statutory bodies under the RTI Act, 2005.

s: Which body solely conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities?
x: Local polls are conducted solely by the State Election Commission (Arts. 243-K, 243-ZA), not the ECI.

s: Who was the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes in August 2026?
x: K.S. Jawahar was the AP State SC Commission chairman (August 2026); State SC/ST Commissions are set up under State laws.

s: Which one of the following bodies was established first?
o: Public Service Commission at the central level
x: The predecessor of the UPSC, the Public Service Commission, was established in 1926. The Federal Public Service Commission followed under the Government of India Act, 1935, and the UPSC came into existence in 1950.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age to 18?
x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18; it was first exercised in the 1989 general election.

s:
Arrange the following institutions in chronological order of their establishment:
A. NITI Aayog
B. National Development Council
C. Planning Commission
D. Inter-State Council
x: The Planning Commission came in 1950, the NDC in 1952, the Inter-State Council in 1990 and NITI Aayog in 2015. The order is C, B, D, A.

s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes were split by which Amendment?
x: The 65th CAA created a joint SC/ST Commission; the 89th CAA, 2003 split it into the NCSC and NCST.

s: The joint National Commission for SCs and STs was given constitutional status by which Amendment?
x: The 65th CAA created the joint SC/ST Commission, later split by the 89th CAA, 2003.

s: Before the 102nd Amendment, the NCBC was a statutory body under an Act of which year?
x: The NCBC was statutory under a 1993 Act and became constitutional (Art. 338-B) by the 102nd CAA, 2018.

s: Under which Act was the Federal Public Service Commission set up?
x: The Public Service Commission of 1926 became the Federal PSC under the GoI Act 1935 and the UPSC in 1950.

s: In which year was the first Public Service Commission set up in India?
x: The Public Service Commission was set up in 1926; it became the Federal PSC (1935) and then the UPSC (1950).

s: The Securities and Exchange Board of India, set up as a non-statutory body in 1988, got statutory powers in which year?
x: SEBI was set up in 1988 by a Government resolution and became statutory under the SEBI Act on 30 January 1992.

s: VVPAT was first used in 2013 in which election?
x: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland on 4 September 2013.

s: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
x: Sukumar Sen led the Election Commission; M.C. Setalvad headed the first Law Commission of independent India.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission?
x: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 with K.C. Neogy as Chairman.

s: Who chaired the first Law Commission of India constituted in 1834?
x: The first Law Commission, constituted in 1834, was chaired by Lord Macaulay.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Lok Sabha Ethics Committee – First such committee by any Indian legislature
Public Accounts Committee – First set up in 1921
Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee – Constituted in 1997
x: The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee (1997) was the first in any Indian legislature; the Lok Sabha one came in 2000.

s: Who was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India?
x: V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman CEC; Sukumar Sen was the first CEC.

s: Who was the first Vice-Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: Nehru chaired the Planning Commission with Gulzarilal Nanda as deputy; Arvind Panagariya was NITI Aayog's first Vice-Chairman.

s:
Consider the following about the First Official Language Commission:
1. It was established in 1955.
2. It was headed by B.G. Kher.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The First Official Language Commission was set up in 1955 under B.G. Kher.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission?
x: Justice Ranganath Misra was the first Chairman of the NHRC, set up in 1993.

s: Who was the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog?
x: Arvind Panagariya was NITI Aayog's first Vice-Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda was the Planning Commission's first.

s: Which was the first language to be declared a Classical Language in India?
x: Tamil was the first language declared a Classical Language in India.

s: How many members, including the Chairman, does the Finance Commission have?
x: The Finance Commission has five members: a Chairman and four others.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NITI Aayog?
o: The Prime Minister is its Chairperson
Its Governing Council includes all Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of UTs
Its Governing Council consists only of Union Cabinet Ministers and Governors
It was set up by a Cabinet Resolution
x: NITI Aayog's Governing Council includes all CMs and LGs of UTs, not only Union Ministers and Governors.

s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that the National Development Council be given constitutional status under Article 263 and renamed as what?
x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended constitutional status for the NDC under Article 263 and proposed the name National Economic and Development Council.

s: From which year did all Union Cabinet Ministers become members of the National Development Council?
x: The NDC was created by executive resolution; all Union Cabinet Ministers became members from 1967.

s: On which date was NITI Aayog established through a Cabinet Resolution?
x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet Resolution of 1 January 2015; the Planning Commission by one of 15 March 1950.

s: After how many years is the Law Commission of India reconstituted?
x: The Law Commission is constituted by executive notification every 3 years; the 23rd runs from 1 Sep 2024 to 31 Aug 2027.

s: Which of the following is an advisory body that studies law reform and submits its reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice?
x: The Law Commission is an advisory research body set up by executive notification; it reports to the Law Ministry.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Law Commission of India:
1. It is constituted by an executive notification for a term of three years.
2. It is a quasi-judicial body.
3. It submits its reports to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Law Commission is set up by notification every three years; it is advisory, not quasi-judicial, and reports to the Law Ministry.

s: To whom is the report of a Joint State Public Service Commission submitted?
x: A JSPSC reports to each Governor concerned, and the report is laid before each State Legislature.

s: The report of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is submitted to the President and:
o: submitted to the Inter-State Council for approval
laid only before the Lok Sabha
laid before Parliament and sent to the States
laid only before the concerned State Legislatures
x: Under Article 350B, the report of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is submitted to the President, laid before Parliament and also sent to the concerned States.

s: The UPSC annual report is laid before Parliament with a memorandum explaining what?
o: Cases where its advice was not accepted
Vacancies in the All India Services
x: Under Article 323 the report goes to the President and is laid before Parliament with a memorandum on non-acceptance of advice.

s: Which of the following considers the annual reports of constitutional bodies such as the CAG, Finance Commission and UPSC?
x: Both Houses consider these reports; the Rajya Sabha has equal status with the Lok Sabha here.

s:
Consider the following statements about the report of a Joint State Public Service Commission:
1. It is submitted to each Governor concerned.
2. It is laid before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: A JSPSC reports to each Governor concerned, and the report is laid before each State Legislature, not Parliament.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the report of the Finance Commission laid before Parliament?
x: Under Article 281 the President lays the FC report before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum.

s: Under which Article does the UPSC present its annual report to the President?
x: Under Article 323 the UPSC reports to the President, who lays it before Parliament with a memorandum on cases of non-acceptance.

s: Under which Article are the CAG's reports on the accounts of the Union submitted to the President and laid before Parliament?
x: Article 151: CAG reports on Union accounts go to the President (State accounts to the Governor) and are laid before the legislature.

s: Where is the headquarters of IRDAI located?
x: IRDAI, set up in April 2000, is headquartered in Hyderabad; SEBI and RBI are in Mumbai.

s: In 2015, to what level was the FDI cap in the insurance sector raised?
x: The insurance FDI cap rose from 26% (2000) to 49% (2015), 74% (2021) and 100% (2025-26).

s: What does Section 16A, inserted in the IRDA Act by the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025, create?
x: The 2025 Act inserted Section 16A in the IRDA Act to create the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund; it also allows up to 100% FDI in insurers.

s: Which accounting standards replaced IGAAP for insurers?
x: Ind AS 117 and Ind AS 109 replaced IGAAP for insurers, and IRDAI enforces their adoption.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Domestic Systemically Important Insurers for FY 2025–26?
o: General Insurance Corporation of India Re
x: The Domestic Systemically Important Insurers for FY 2025–26 are LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance. HDFC Bank is listed among the D-SIBs, not the D-SIIs.

s: Who headed the seven-member expert panel set up in February 2025 to review IRDAI regulations?
x: A seven-member panel under Dinesh Khara was set up in February 2025 to review IRDAI regulations.

s: From which provision does IRDAI get its regulation-making power?
x: Section 114A of the Insurance Act, 1938 gives IRDAI its regulation-making power; Section 16A of the IRDA Act creates the Policyholders' fund.

s: When was IRDAI, created under the IRDA Act, 1999, set up?
x: IRDAI was set up in April 2000 under the IRDA Act, 1999 (headquartered at Hyderabad); 1994 is the year of the Malhotra Committee report.

s: On whose recommendation was the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) set up?
x: The Malhotra Committee (set up 1993, reported 1994) recommended an insurance regulator and private entry; IRDA came under the IRDA Act, 1999.

s:
Consider the following statements about IRDAI:
1. It is a statutory body under the IRDA Act, 1999.
2. It was set up on the recommendation of the Malhotra Committee.
3. Its headquarters is at Mumbai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: IRDAI is statutory (IRDA Act, 1999) and came from the Malhotra Committee's advice, but its headquarters is at Hyderabad, not Mumbai.

s: Which Act, passed in December 2025, allows up to 100 per cent FDI in the insurance sector?
o: Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025
x: The Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025, passed on 17 December 2025, allows up to 100% FDI in insurance.

s: In which year did the Malhotra Committee on insurance sector reforms submit its report?
x: The Malhotra Committee was set up in 1993 and reported in 1994; it recommended private entry and an insurance regulator.

s: In 2021, to what level was the FDI cap in the insurance sector raised?
x: The insurance FDI cap went from 26% (2000) to 49% (2015), 74% (2021) and 100% (2025-26).

s: With which regulator is the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund under Section 16A of the IRDA Act linked?
x: Section 16A, added by the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025, creates the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund under IRDAI.

s: SEBI was first set up by a resolution in 1988. In which year did it get statutory status?
x: SEBI became a statutory body under the SEBI Act, 1992.

s: The Securities and Exchange Board of India replaced which of the following authorities?
o: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
x: SEBI replaced the Controller of Capital Issues in the regulation of the capital market.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SEBI?
o: SEBI can investigate, summon persons and impose penalties
Appeals against SEBI's orders lie first to the NCLAT
Appeals against SEBI's orders lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and then to the Supreme Court
Since 2014, orders of IRDAI and PFRDA are also appealable to the SAT
x: Appeals against SEBI's orders go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) and then to the Supreme Court, not the NCLAT.

s: With which of the following is SEBI's SWAGAT-FI associated?
o: A single-window framework for trusted FPIs and FVCIs
A pension scheme for informal workers
x: SWAGAT-FI is a single-window framework for trusted Foreign Portfolio Investors and Foreign Venture Capital Investors.

s: Where does an appeal against an order of SEBI lie first?
x: SEBI orders go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and then to the Supreme Court, not to the NCLAT.

s:
Consider the following statements about SEBI:
1. It has quasi-judicial powers to investigate, summon and impose penalties.
2. Orders of IRDAI and PFRDA are also appealable to the Securities Appellate Tribunal since 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: SEBI has quasi-judicial powers, and since 2014 IRDAI and PFRDA orders also go to SAT.

s: When was the Forward Markets Commission merged into SEBI?
x: The Forward Markets Commission, which regulated commodities, was merged into SEBI in September 2015.

s: Under which law was the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) established on 1 October 2016?
x: IBBI is the regulator under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

s: To whom does PFRDA's NPS e-Shramik seek to extend pension coverage?
x: NPS e-Shramik extends pension coverage to informal workers.

s: On the dissolution of BIFR on 1 December 2016, to which bodies were its cases transferred?
x: BIFR, constituted under SICA 1985, was dissolved on 1 December 2016 and its cases moved to NCLT/NCLAT under the IBC.

s: Which of the following pairs (regulator – establishing law) is correctly matched?
x: IBBI was established under the IBC, 2016; RBI rests on the RBI Act, 1934, IRDAI on the IRDA Act, 1999 and IFSCA on the IFSCA Act, 2019.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The RBI was set up on 1 April 1935 and was nationalised in 1949. PFRDA became statutory from 2014, IBBI was set up on 1 October 2016, and IFSCA on 27 April 2020.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: IBBI — New Delhi — Ministry of Finance
PFRDA — New Delhi — Ministry of Finance
x: IBBI is headquartered in New Delhi but comes under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, not the Ministry of Finance. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) located?
x: IFSCA is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar. It functions under the Ministry of Finance.

s: Which financial regulator functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs?
x: IBBI is the only one of these regulators under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; the others are under Finance.

s: When was the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) set up?
x: IFSCA was set up on 27 April 2020 under the IFSCA Act, 2019; it is the newest financial regulator.

s: Which financial regulator promotes FinTech through regulatory and innovation sandboxes at GIFT City?
x: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), based at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, promotes FinTech through regulatory and innovation sandboxes.

s: PFRDA worked as an interim body from 2003. In which year did it become a statutory body?
x: PFRDA got statutory status in 2014 under the PFRDA Act, 2013.

s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the setting up of these regulators?
1. IRDAI
2. IBBI
3. RBI
4. IFSCA
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: RBI came in 1935, IRDAI in 2000, IBBI in 2016 and IFSCA in 2020; RBI is the oldest and IFSCA the newest.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Regulating and supervising banks and NBFCs
Issuing the one-rupee note and coins
x: The Ministry of Finance issues the one-rupee note and coins. RBI functions include monetary authority, foreign-exchange management under FEMA, and regulation and supervision of banks and NBFCs.

s: How many Upper-Layer NBFCs, including Tata Sons, did the RBI name for 2026-27?
x: The RBI named 17 Upper-Layer NBFCs for 2026-27; they must list within 3 years.

s: Under which Act does the RBI act as the manager of foreign exchange?
x: The RBI is the forex manager under FEMA 1999.

s: Who issues the ₹1 note and coins in India?
x: The RBI issues currency except the ₹1 note and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance.

s: Why was the Public Debt Management Cell set up?
o: To manage foreign exchange under FEMA, 1999
To reduce the RBI's conflict of interest between monetary policy and debt management
To insure bank deposits up to a fixed limit
x: The Public Debt Management Cell was set up to separate debt management from the RBI's monetary policy role and reduce the conflict of interest.

s: Within how many years must the Upper-Layer NBFCs named by the RBI for 2026-27 get listed?
x: The RBI named 17 Upper-Layer NBFCs, including Tata Sons, for 2026-27; they must list within 3 years.

s: For how many years are the external members of the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee appointed by the Centre?
x: The six-member MPC has three external members appointed by the Centre for 4 years; the Governor chairs it with a casting vote.

s: Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934, how often does the Centre, in consultation with the RBI, set the inflation target?
x: Section 45ZA lets the Centre, consulting the RBI, set the inflation target every five years.

s: What is the inflation target under India's flexible inflation-targeting framework?
o: 6% headline CPI with no tolerance band
4% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
2% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 4%
4% WPI with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
x: The target is 4% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%. The framework uses CPI-Combined, not WPI, as the specified measure.

s: Which of the following correctly states the hierarchy of objectives under the inflation-targeting framework?
o: Price stability is primary and growth is secondary
Growth is primary and price stability is secondary
Fiscal consolidation is primary and price stability is optional
Exchange-rate stability is primary and growth is excluded
x: Price stability is the primary objective, while growth is treated as a secondary objective.

s: India's flexible inflation-targeting framework, adopted in 2016, was based on the recommendation of which committee?
x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended inflation targeting, adopted in 2016 with a 4% CPI-Combined target. The Narasimham Committee dealt with banking reforms, the Malhotra Committee with insurance reforms, and the Raghuram Rajan Committee with financial-sector reforms, not the inflation-targeting framework.

s: Under Section 45ZN of the RBI Act, for how long must inflation stay outside the band before the RBI reports to the Centre?
x: If the band is breached for 3 consecutive quarters, the RBI reports reasons, remedies and time to restore to the Centre.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee?
o: It is a statutory body under the RBI Act, 1934
The Governor chairs it and has a casting vote
It has 3 RBI members and 4 external members
x: The MPC has 6 members: 3 from the RBI and 3 external members appointed by the Centre for 4 years.

s: What is the base year of the headline CPI used as the nominal anchor of India's inflation target?
x: The nominal anchor is headline CPI-Combined with base year 2024.

s: Who chairs the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC), set up in 2010?
x: The non-statutory FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and handles financial stability and inter-regulatory coordination.

s: What is the nature of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC), set up in 2010?
o: Statutory body under the RBI Act
Statutory body under the SEBI Act
x: FSDC is a non-statutory apex body set up in 2010 and chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

s: Who was the chairman of the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission?
x: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna.

s: The FSLRC proposed a Unified Financial Agency merging SEBI, FMC and IRDA with which other regulator?
x: The Unified Financial Agency was to merge SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA; the RBI was to keep banking and payments.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, towards what kind of regulation are RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA moving?
x: The Economic Survey 2025–26, under the theme ‘Refining the Regulatory Touch’, stated that these regulators are moving towards anticipatory regulation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a role of the Financial Stability and Development Council?
x: FSDC handles financial stability, inter-regulatory coordination, macro-prudential supervision and financial literacy; the repo rate is fixed by the RBI's MPC.

s: In which year did the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission submit its report?
x: FSLRC, chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, was set up in 2011 and reported in 2013.

s: Who chairs the sub-committee of the Financial Stability and Development Council?
x: The FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, but its sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor.

s: Which of the following was NOT proposed by the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission (FSLRC)?
o: A separate constitutional court for financial disputes
x: The FSLRC proposed an Indian Financial Code, a Public Debt Management Agency and a Financial Redress Agency, but not a constitutional court for financial disputes.

s: Which body regulates mutual funds in India?
x: SEBI regulates listed companies, intermediaries and mutual funds.

s: Since 2019, which body regulates housing finance companies in India?
x: Regulation of housing finance companies shifted to the RBI in 2019; the NHB remains the apex housing refinancer.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its present regulator?
x: NBFCs are regulated by the RBI. Merchant banks, venture-capital funds and brokers are under SEBI; insurers are under IRDAI; chit funds are under state governments.

s: Who regulates chit funds in India?
x: Chit funds are regulated by State governments under the Chit Funds Act 1982, not by the RBI.

s: In which year was the National Housing Bank set up?
x: The NHB was set up in 1988 under the NHB Act, 1987; the Centre took full ownership of it in 2019.

s: Which regulator oversees the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID), set up under the NaBFID Act, 2021?
x: NaBFID, created under the NaBFID Act, 2021, is under RBI oversight.

s: Under which ministry does the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority, a statutory authority under the Companies Act, 2013, function?
x: IEPF Authority is a statutory authority under the Companies Act, 2013, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), set up in 1978, is a wholly-owned subsidiary of which body?
x: DICGC is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the RBI, not the Finance Ministry; it insures bank deposits but not NBFC deposits.

s: Under which provision was the RBI's Banking Ombudsman Scheme, started on 14 June 1995, framed?
x: The quasi-judicial Banking Ombudsman scheme began on 14 June 1995 under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act.

s: Which body oversees auditing and accounting standards under the Companies Act, 2013?
x: The National Financial Reporting Authority oversees auditing and accounting standards under the Companies Act, 2013.

s: When was the Competition Commission of India established?
x: The Competition Act commenced on 31 March 2003 and the CCI was set up on 14 October 2003.

s: From 26 May 2017, to which body do appeals against orders of the Competition Commission of India lie?
o: High Court directly in every case
x: NCLAT became the appellate forum for CCI matters from 26 May 2017. Earlier, appeals lay to COMPAT, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

s: Which of the following did the Competition Act, 2002 replace?
o: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 and CCI
Companies Act, 1956 and Company Law Board
x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 and its MRTP Commission.

s: On what ground did the CCI act against WhatsApp's 2021 privacy policy?
x: The WhatsApp case concerned abuse of dominant position; combinations means reviewing mergers and acquisitions.

s: Which enterprises does the proposed Digital Competition Bill seek to pre-regulate?
o: Digital enterprises registered outside India alone
All online platforms irrespective of their size
x: The proposed Digital Competition Bill would pre-regulate Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises.

s: What does the ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold for combinations under competition law target?
x: The threshold targets start-up 'killer acquisitions' that may escape traditional scrutiny; combinations are mergers and acquisitions, not cartels.

s: What is the present composition of the Competition Commission of India?
