o: A Chairperson and two to six other members appointed by the Central Government
A Chairperson and exactly six members appointed by the Supreme Court
Only a Chairperson and one member appointed by the President
A Chairperson and two to six members appointed by the State Governments
x: The current composition is a Chairperson and two to six other members, all appointed by the Central Government.

s: Under which Act is the Competition Commission of India a statutory body?
x: The CCI is statutory under the Competition Act, 2002 (amended 2007), under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; the MRTP Act, 1969 is the law it replaced.

s: Before 26 May 2017, to which body did appeals against CCI orders lie?
x: Appeals went to COMPAT until 26 May 2017, when the NCLAT took over.

s: Under which Ministry does the Competition Commission of India function?
x: The CCI, a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002, works under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

s: What penalty did the Competition Commission of India impose on Meta/WhatsApp for abuse of dominant position?
x: The CCI fined Meta/WhatsApp ₹213.14 crore over its 2021 privacy policy; the NCLAT upheld the abuse finding.

s: Under the original Competition Act, 2002, up to how many members besides the Chairperson could the Competition Commission of India have?
x: The original 2002 Act allowed up to 10 members; now the CCI has a Chairperson and 2 to 6 members.

s: When was TRAI established?
x: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India was set up on 20 February 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997.

s: Which body hears telecom disputes and appeals, separate from TRAI's regulatory role?
x: TRAI regulates tariffs, interconnection and quality of service, while TDSAT handles telecom disputes and appeals.

s: By which law was the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT), set up in May 2000, created?
x: TDSAT was created in May 2000 by the TRAI (Amendment) Act, which separated adjudication from TRAI's regulatory role. There is no separate 'TDSAT Act, 2000'; that is a common trap. The IT Act, 2000 only adds appeals that TDSAT hears, and the Telegraph Act, 1885 is the old telegraph law.

s: When was the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) set up?
x: TDSAT was set up in May 2000 and also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.

s: Besides TRAI orders, under which Acts does TDSAT also hear appeals?
x: TDSAT also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)?
x: TRAI regulates tariffs, interconnection and quality of service; disputes and appeals go to TDSAT.

s: Which TRAI app, revamped in August 2026, lets users rate call quality?
x: TRAI revamped its MyCall app for rating call quality in August 2026, after its DND and MySpeed apps.

s: What happened to the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill after its introduction in the Lok Sabha in December 2025?
o: Referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament
x: The VBSA Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025 and referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament; it has not been passed.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three councils proposed under the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
x: The proposed Bill provides for Regulatory, Accreditation and Standards Councils. A Funding Council is not among the three councils listed.

s: Which of the following Acts would NOT be repealed by the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
x: The VBSA Bill would repeal the UGC, AICTE and NCTE Acts; the National Medical Commission Act is not among them.

s: In which year was FSSAI, under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, set up?
x: The Food Safety and Standards Act is of 2006; FSSAI was set up in 2008.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: FSSAI — Director General of Health Services as its administrative ministry
FSSAI — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
FSSAI — Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
x: FSSAI is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is not under the Director General of Health Services. Eat Right India was launched in 2018.

s: Which one of the following was among the laws or orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006?
x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was among the eight laws and orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

s: From 1 July 2019, in which of the following are food businesses prohibited from wrapping food?
x: From 1 July 2019, recycled plastics and newspaper may not be used to wrap food.

s: In which year was FSSAI's Eat Right India movement launched?
x: Eat Right India (2018) is FSSAI's movement for safe, healthy and sustainable food.

s: Under the 2026 FSSAI reforms, up to what turnover does basic registration cover food businesses?
x: Registration now covers turnover up to ₹1.5 crore (earlier ₹12 lakh); above ₹50 crore needs a Central licence.

s: Which of the following administers FSSAI?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: FSSAI is an independent statutory authority administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not the DGHS.

s: How many laws and orders were consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006?
x: The FSS Act, 2006 consolidated eight laws and orders, including the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

s: Under the 2026 FSSAI reforms, what validity do food licences and registrations get?
x: The 2026 FSSAI reforms gave licences and registrations perpetual validity.

s: Under the 2026 FSSAI tiers, food businesses above what turnover need a Central licence?
x: Registration covers up to ₹1.5 crore, a State licence ₹1.5-50 crore, and a Central licence above ₹50 crore.

s: Which of the following is a statutory body under the Ministry of Power?
o: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board
x: CEA, APTEL and CERC are statutory bodies under the Ministry of Power.

s: When was the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board, under the PNGRB Act 2006, set up?
x: The PNGRB Act is of 2006, but the Board was set up on 1 October 2007.

s:
Match List-I (Act) with List-II (Year of enactment):
List-I
A. TRAI Act
B. Competition Act
C. Electricity Act
D. Food Safety and Standards Act
List-II
1. 2003
2. 2006
3. 1997
4. 2002
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: TRAI Act is of 1997, Competition Act 2002, Electricity Act 2003 and Food Safety and Standards Act 2006.

s: In which year was the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act enacted?
x: The PNGRB Act was enacted in 2006; the Board itself was set up on 1 October 2007.

s: Under which Ministry does the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA), set up in 2009, function?
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
x: AERA was set up in 2009 under the AERA Act, 2008, and is under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: APTEL — appeals against CERC and SERC orders
x: APTEL hears appeals against orders of CERC and SERCs. CERC deals with inter-State matters, while SERCs deal mainly with intra-State tariffs and consumer protection.

s: Who removes the chairperson of a sectoral regulator, on grounds listed in the parent Act and after a hearing?
o: President on a Supreme Court reference
x: Removal is by the Central Government only on grounds specified in the parent Act and after the person has been heard.

s: Who heads the search-cum-selection committee for the CCI chairperson?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Justice of India or a nominee
x: Chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government on a search-cum-selection committee's recommendation; for the CCI it is headed by the CJI or a nominee.

s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for removing a regulator's chairperson?
o: Conviction for an offence of moral turpitude
x: Removal is by the Central Government on grounds in the parent Act, such as insolvency, moral turpitude, incapacity or abuse of position; not by Parliament.

s: Which body regulates inter-State electricity matters?
x: CERC handles inter-State electricity matters; SERCs handle intra-State tariffs.

s: Under which Act was APERC constituted in 1999?
x: APERC was constituted in 1999 under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.

s: To which tribunal do appeals against orders of CERC, SERCs and PNGRB lie?
x: APTEL, set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act, 2003, hears appeals from CERC, SERCs and PNGRB.

s:
Consider the following statements about electricity regulators:
1. SERCs fix intra-State electricity tariffs.
2. Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, APERC stayed joint regulator for not more than six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: SERCs handle intra-State tariffs, and APERC was joint regulator for up to six months until separate SERCs were formed.

s: Which body is the regulator of carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
o: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board
Securities and Exchange Board of India
x: CERC regulates carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, which is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

s: Which of the following pairs (regulator – function) is correctly matched?
o: AERA – Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: PNGRB works under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and regulates City Gas Distribution networks; it does not regulate electricity transmission.

s: What does the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) regulate?
x: AERA regulates airport tariffs (aeronautical charges) at major airports.

s: In July 2026, how many Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh did PNGRB approve for City Gas Distribution?
x: PNGRB approved 10 Geographical Areas in AP for City Gas Distribution; East Godavari has the most connections.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the most City Gas Distribution connections?
x: Of the 10 PNGRB-approved Geographical Areas in AP, East Godavari has the most CGD connections.

s: Under the DPDP Rules, 2025, the Data Protection Board of India has how many members?
x: The DPDP Rules, 2025 provide for a four-member Data Protection Board under the DPDP Act, 2023.

s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, what is the maximum penalty the Data Protection Board can impose?
o: Rs 50 crore, with imprisonment up to 3 years
Rs 500 crore, with imprisonment up to 7 years
x: The Board can impose penalties of up to Rs 250 crore, and the Act provides no imprisonment. So the options with imprisonment are wrong, and Rs 50 crore or Rs 25 crore understate the ceiling.

s: Before which forum can an order of the Data Protection Board of India be challenged in appeal?
o: The TDSAT within 60 days, with a further appeal to the Supreme Court
x: Appeals against the Board's orders go to the TDSAT within 60 days, and from there to the Supreme Court. The claim that appeals go directly to the Supreme Court is a known wrong statement. The High Court and NCLAT are not the appellate forums under the DPDP Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Data Protection Board of India?
o: It is an independent adjudicatory body
Its members are appointed on a Selection Committee's recommendation
It can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore
x: The Board can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore but cannot order imprisonment.

s: Which provision of the RTI Act was amended by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, widening the exemption for personal information?
x: Critics point out that the DPDP Act amends Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act, giving a wider exemption for personal information.

s: With which issue was the National Green Tribunal's order on rat-hole mining in Meghalaya mainly concerned?
o: Air pollution caused by diesel vehicles
x: The 2014 ban on rat-hole mining in Meghalaya addressed unscientific and unsafe coal mining.

s: Which problem did the National Green Tribunal's 2015 ban on diesel vehicles older than 10 years in Delhi-NCR mainly address?
x: The 2015 Delhi-NCR order on diesel vehicles older than 10 years addressed air pollution.

s: Where is the southern zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
x: NGT zonal benches are Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai (South); the principal bench is New Delhi.

s: Where does an appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lie?
x: NGT orders are appealable directly to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

s: The National Green Tribunal must dispose of a case within how long of its filing?
x: The NGT Act mandates disposal within 6 months of filing.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. It became operational on 18 October 2010.
2. Its civil jurisdiction covers seven Acts listed in Schedule I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the NGT began on 18 October 2010 and Schedule I lists 7 Acts, including the Water Act, 1974.

s: In 2016, for what did the National Green Tribunal fine the Art of Living?
x: The Art of Living's World Culture Festival damaged the Yamuna floodplain, and the NGT fined it in 2016.

s: Under which Act was the National Green Tribunal set up?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
x: The NGT was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 and became operational on 18 October 2010.

s: Where is the principal bench of the National Green Tribunal located?
x: The NGT's principal bench is at New Delhi; Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai are its zonal benches.

s: Which of the following is NOT a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
x: The four zonal benches are Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai; there is no NGT bench at Hyderabad.

s: In which State did the National Green Tribunal ban rat-hole mining in 2014?
x: In 2014 the NGT banned rat-hole coal mining in Meghalaya as unscientific and unsafe.

s: Which organisation did the National Green Tribunal direct in August 2023 to plant at least 10,000 trees in Uttarakhand within two months?
x: The NGT (Aug 2023) directed the Border Roads Organisation to plant at least 10,000 trees in Uttarakhand within one month (the stem's 'two months' is wrong; the key BRO stands).

s: The preamble of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 refers to the right to a healthy environment as part of which Article of the Constitution?
x: The NGT Act's preamble notes that the right to a healthy environment is read as part of the right to life under Article 21.

s: How many full-time Judicial Members can the National Green Tribunal have under the NGT Act, 2010?
x: Section 4 of the NGT Act provides a full-time Chairperson, and 10 to 20 Judicial Members and 10 to 20 Expert Members.

s: Which of the following Acts is NOT in Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010?
x: Schedule I lists seven Acts, including the Forest (Conservation), Biological Diversity and Public Liability Insurance Acts; the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 is kept out.

s: Which Amendment inserted Part XIVA (Articles 323A and 323B) into the Constitution?
x: Part XIVA was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 and came into force on 1 March 1977.

s: Under Article 323A, who can set up administrative tribunals for public service matters?
x: Only Parliament can create a 323A tribunal; under 323B both Parliament and State Legislatures can act.

s: Which of the following is NOT a subject listed under Article 323B?
x: Public service matters fall under Article 323A; taxation, land reforms and rent are Article 323B subjects.

s: From which date did Part XIVA (Tribunals) of the Constitution come into force?
x: Part XIVA, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, came into force on 1 March 1977.

s: Under Article 323B, who can set up tribunals for matters such as taxation, land reforms and rent?
x: Article 323A tribunals can be created only by Parliament; Article 323B tribunals by both Parliament and State Legislatures.

s: Under which Act was the Central Administrative Tribunal set up?
x: CAT was set up under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, made under Article 323A(1).

s: After L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), where does an appeal against a CAT order lie first?
o: Division Bench of the High Court
x: L. Chandra Kumar held judicial review under Articles 226/227 to be basic structure, so CAT orders go to a High Court Division Bench, then the Supreme Court.

s: In L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), the power of judicial review of High Courts under which Articles was held to be part of the basic structure?
